{"triples": [{"subject": "BERT", "predicate": "uses", "object": "vector norm", "object_type": "Concept", "source_sentence": "Given that we know that BERT is a contextual encoder, and that its self-attention uses the vector norm to control the levels of contribution from less informative words , we suspect that this gives it the capabilities to accurately model these short-distance dependencies and word co-occurence probabilities, concepts which strongly correspond to local contextual incongruity."}, {"subject": "BERT", "predicate": "uses", "object": "norm", "object_type": "Concept", "source_sentence": "BERT is evidently capable of encoding this signal well, and seems to be using its norm to supplement the encoding of the phenomenon in such a way that it positions sentences exhibiting local contextual incongruity closer to the origin, relative to sentences that do not contain it."}, {"subject": "BERT", "predicate": "uses", "object": "norm", "object_type": "Concept", "source_sentence": "Furthermore, BERT's ability to model incongruity via the norm could essentially be frequency-based, similar to how some word embeddings encode word frequency in the norm."}, {"subject": "GloVe", "predicate": "uses", "object": "norm", "object_type": "Concept", "source_sentence": "In contrast, GloVe is a static encoder and exhibits no indication that it stores this information in the norm, or indeed any ability to accurately model this phenomenon at all, but uses the norm to store surface-level and syntactic information."}]}
